pr_title: feat: Add support for `IO[bytes]` and `bytes` in `scan_{...}` functions
pr_body:
This PR adds support for the `bytes` and `IO[bytes]` interface to all `scan_{parquet, csv, ...}` functions.

Since the same code was being touched. This PR also fixes #18581.

Fixes #4950.
Fixes #12617.
pr_comments: Putting this back into draft for a second. I want to try to remove the specialized `read_{_}` impls as well with this PR now so I made it possible to pass opened files. This did create some further problems, which I still need to fix.

issue_context.title: Incorrect/mismatched LazyFrame schema resolution between `collect` and `collect_schema`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile

import polars as pl


ctx = pl.SQLContext()


with NamedTemporaryFile() as f:
    f.write(b"a,b,c\n1,2,3\n4,5,6")
    f.flush()

    ctx.register("test", pl.scan_csv(f.name))
    lf = ctx.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS x FROM test")

    lazy_schema = lf.collect_schema()
    actual_schema = lf.collect().schema


expected = pl.Schema({"x": pl.UInt32})


# The lazy schema is correct
assert lazy_schema == expected
# The actual schema is incorrect (column name is `len`, not `x`)
assert actual_schema == expected

```


### Log output

```shell
$ POLARS_VERBOSE=1 python bug.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/jcristharif/Code/ibis/bug.py", line 26, in <module>
    assert actual_schema == expected
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError
```


### Issue description

Sometimes when executing SQL against a lazyframe the resulting column names don't match (the alias is ignored). If I swap out the `scan_csv` for a `read_csv` (or an in-memory `DataFrame`) things work properly.

### Expected behavior

SQL aliases to be properly respected.

comments:
@ritchie46, @nameexhaustion: FYI, looks like this one isn't SQL related - can reproduce using standard (non-SQL) operations, as below (updated the issue title accordingly).

Schema resolution is correct when going through `collect_schema`, but incorrect on a standard `collect`:
```python
from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile
import polars as pl

with NamedTemporaryFile() as f:
    f.write(b"a,b,c\n1,2,3\n4,5,6")
    f.flush()

    # :: INCORRECT schema resolution ("collect")
    lf = pl.scan_csv(f.name)
    print(lf.select(pl.count().alias("n")).collect())  
    # shape: (1, 1)
    # ┌─────┐
    # │ len │
    # │ --- │
    # │ u32 │
    # ╞═════╡
    # │ 2   │
    # └─────┘

    # :: CORRECT schema resolution ("collect_schema")
    print(lf.select(pl.count().alias("n")).collect_schema())  
    # Schema({'n': UInt32})
```

review_comments: HiveOptions::default sets enabled to `Some(true)` this is problematic. So I changed it here.
We remove the options here, basically because the memory map options do not do anything anymore
